seed.note: Split-Flap Concourse was dealt as a catalog challenger on this key and chosen by the user over the assigned grounded direction. Persisted so a later session can verify the roll.

flap-shadow.note: Declared in :root, currently unreferenced. Lit cells author their own two-stop gradient.

amber-bright.note: Hover-only lift on filled amber. A literal in component rules, not a :root custom property.

amber-dim.note: Declared in :root, currently unreferenced. Amber states brighten on hover rather than dim.

amber-ink.note: The only text color permitted on an amber fill.

red.note: Declared and deliberately used nowhere. Reserved for a stopped, cancelled, or delayed state.

steel-deep.note: Declared in :root, currently unreferenced. The darkest step of the steel ramp.

lamp-green.note: The one hue outside the stated palette. Confined to the 0.6rem service lamp; never text, fill, or border.

seam.note: The 1px black line at 50% height of every flap cell and wordmark cell.

cell-edge.note: Declared in :root, currently unreferenced. Lit cells use 0.08 and ghosts 0.045 inline.

narrative.overview:
The world is a rail concourse departure board: matte flap black with a real seam through every character cell, brushed steel frames and rivets, paint-white condensed caps in fixed-width cells, amber reserved for live status. A career is read the way a hall reads a schedule, two boards running at once, revenue departing and software arriving. The board is a built object with hardware, not a dark theme with a monospace font.

The direction is recorded on concept seed key a9d5223a (scope: direction, mode: persuade), dealt as a catalog challenger against the assigned grounded direction and chosen by the user over it. That key is persisted so a later session can verify the roll rather than re-derive the world.

Density is high and horizontal. Every unit of information is a row in a table, so the page has no cards, no tiles, and no metric grid. Depth comes only from the steel frame and the recess behind it. The refusals are part of the world: no scroll-reveal counters, no terminal boot overlay, no glassmorphism, no gradient mesh, no hover lift.
keyCharacteristics: Matte black panels held in four-sided brushed steel, riveted at the corners and along the rails
A 1px seam through the middle of every character cell, the single detail that makes the board a board
Amber is the only saturated color, and it means live, current, or actionable
Rows are the only container; every dataset is a real semantic table
Exactly two authored motion beats, both of them the board settling
Condensed caps for board voice, plain Barlow for anything a human reads as a sentence

rules.name: The Reserved Red Rule
rules.body: Red is declared and spent on nothing. It belongs to a stopped state only. No error text, no destructive button, and no accent may claim it; if red appears anywhere other than a halted row, the system has been broken.

rules.name: The Amber Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Amber means live, current, or actionable, and nothing else. A completed row is steel outline; an in-build row is steel outline with white text. If a screen has more than one amber region competing for the eye, one of them is decorative and must be demoted to steel.

rules.name: The Two Materials Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are matte flap black; structure is brushed steel. There is no third material. The only translucency in the system is the sticky header's near-opaque scrim (rgba(13,13,15,0.94) with a 10px backdrop blur); nothing else is frosted, glassy, or tinted.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: The condensed face ships only 600 and 700. Flap-voice elements that declare no weight inherit 400 and resolve to 600 by font matching, which is the intended board weight. Never author condensed at 400, 500, or 800; there is no file to serve it and synthesis will not match the painted glyph.

rules.name: The One Matrix Rule
rules.body: A flap panel has one cell size. The hero name and the thesis rows share a single font-size because a board has a single matrix; a headline with a smaller caption underneath is a poster, not a board. The size floor is set by the longest row fitting its panel, not by a comfortable reading size.

rules.name: The Board Voice Rule
rules.body: Condensed is always uppercase and always letterspaced (0.05em to 0.24em). Barlow is always sentence case. A condensed lowercase word or an uppercase paragraph of Barlow is out of world.

rules.name: The Row Rule
rules.body: Rows are the only container. Any new dataset is a table with real th and a caption, not a card grid, not tiles, not a stat row. If a piece of content cannot be expressed as a row, it belongs in the notice board's prose column.

rules.name: The Designed Break Rule
rules.body: Columns never reflow mid-row. At 720px a board restacks into whole labeled records the way a platform sign does. A layout that merely wraps its cells is a bug, not a breakpoint.

rules.name: The Recess Rule
rules.body: Depth belongs to the frame. Panels sit behind steel and everything inside them is flat. A shadow on a row, a status pill, or a button is out of world.

rules.name: The Real Surface Rule
rules.body: Steel is an authored surface, not a gradient. --steel-plate is a 32px SVG data URI: feTurbulence fractal noise at baseFrequency 0.035 0.9 with stitchTiles: stitch, desaturated, at 0.4 opacity over a flat #A9AFB6 base. No baked gradient, because a roll baked into the tile resets at every repeat and puts a ladder of seams down the side rails.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Max radius is 3px, and only on the two non-frame panels. Frames are 0. If a shape needs a radius to look finished, it is the wrong shape for this world.

rules.name: The Two Beats Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two authored motion moments on the page: the board settling on arrival and the last board settling at the close. Not one per section. Anything legible before the motion runs must stay legible if the motion never runs.

rules.name: The Top Hinge Rule
rules.body: A leaf hinges at its top edge and falls through rotateX with real perspective. No scaleY squash, no fade-in-up, no scroll-triggered reveal, no counter tick.

dos: Do put every new dataset in a real <table> with a visually-hidden caption, scope="col" headers, and tabular-nums.
Do wrap any new board in .board-frame so it inherits the steel, the rivets, and the recess. The frame is what makes a surface part of this world.
Do keep amber to live, current, and actionable states, plus the focus ring.
Do build display text out of fixed 0.72em flap cells with a seam, and pad the row with .flap-ghost cells so the matrix reaches the panel edge.
Do mark every flap cell aria-hidden and give its row a .visually-hidden text node carrying the real string.
Do hold radii at 0 (frames), 1px (wordmark), 2px (cells and chrome), 3px (soft panels).
Do self-host any new weight as a latin-subset woff2 in fonts/ with font-display: swap.
Do design the breakpoint: restack whole records, move an element to its own ruled row, or drop a gloss. Six breaks exist (1279, 1080, 860, 720, 480, 359) and each one is a decision.
Do make every new motion legible before it runs and instant under prefers-reduced-motion.
Do use [hidden] for collapsed panels and keep the display: none !important override, because board rows become display: block below 720px.
donts: Don't spend the red token. It is reserved for a stopped state and is used zero times in this build.
Don't introduce cards, tiles, metric grids, or stat boxes. Rows are the only container.
Don't add a third authored motion beat, a scroll-reveal, a counter tick, or a terminal boot overlay.
Don't put a shadow on anything inside a board. Depth belongs to the frame.
Don't author Barlow Condensed at any weight other than 600 or 700; no other file is served.
Don't set condensed type in lowercase or run Barlow prose in uppercase.
Don't size a headline and a caption differently inside the same flap panel. One panel, one matrix, one cell size.
Don't fake steel with a linear-gradient. The frame is the --steel-plate turbulence tile, and a baked gradient bands at every repeat.
Don't stretch a rivet to fit a pitch. The bolt is 7px; the pitch is the 112px tile.
Don't add glass, frost, or gradient-mesh surfaces. The header scrim is the only translucent element in the system.
Don't use glyph icons or an icon font. Icons are inline SVG at 1.75 stroke with square caps and mitered joins.
Don't rely on aria-label on a generic span for an accessible name; render real text into a .visually-hidden node.
